rounding.rule: exact fractions of integers, rounded half up once when written

observed.kind: computed from the observed event rows
observed.day_rule: the day of an event is the UTC date of its JSON timestamp

episodes_of_burst_days.rule: Analysis choice, taken from PSY-008 so that both lessons name the same groups: a burst day has at least burst_day_from events (PSY-008's threshold, above the 99% quantile of its Poisson benchmark), and burst days at most gap_days apart belong to one episode.

lorenz_and_gini.gini_formula: G = sum over i of (2 i - n - 1) x_i / (n T), with the n daily counts sorted in increasing order x_1 <= ... <= x_n and T their total
other_formulas_checked_equal: mean absolute difference between two days / (2 * mean)

mean_and_median.quantile_rule: nearest rank: the p% quantile of n values sorted in increasing order is the value at position ceil(p * n / 100)
mean_and_median.median_rule: the middle value of the n values sorted in increasing order; when n is even, the mean of the two middle values (the nearest-rank 50% quantile would take the lower of the two)

robustness.kind: computed: the same measures under other analysis choices (day boundary, types counted), and the log as the design's deduplication rule would have merged it

day_boundary.note: Analysis choice. The lesson counts days in UTC; each offset recounts them with the day boundary moved by that many hours (the local date of a clock set to UTC plus the offset).

type_subsets.note: Analysis choice: the same measures on the events of one group of types, over the same calendar days.

deduplicated_once_a_day.kind: synthetic: the rule is stated by the design (observed); waking once at the end of each UTC day is assumed, because the driver was never scheduled

poisson_control.kind: synthetic: logs with the observed total and number of days, each event on a day drawn uniformly at random
poisson_control.note: Synthetic logs with the observed number of events and of calendar days and no concentration beyond chance: every event falls on a day chosen uniformly at random, independently of the others. This is a homogeneous Poisson process conditioned on its total.
poisson_control.generator: rng = random.Random(seed); for each log, for each event: day = min(days - 1, int(rng.random() * days))
poisson_control.summary_keys: min, the 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles (nearest rank), the median (nearest rank), max and mean over the logs
poisson_control.comparison_directions: counts of synthetic logs whose value is >= the observed one, except days_needed_for_half, events_on_the_quietest_half_of_days and median_calendar_day (<=)

negative_control.what: the same comparisons after adding the observed log to the batch: each count must rise by exactly 1

capacity.kind: synthetic: an assumed handling rule applied to the observed daily counts; the repository states that the consumer of these triggers was never scheduled, so nothing here was measured
capacity.handling_rule: Each day, after the day's arrivals, at most `capacity` events are handled, oldest first. Events that are not handled wait for the next day. Capacity that is not used on a day is lost. The wait of an event is the number of days between its arrival day and the day it is handled (0 = handled on its arrival day).
capacity.wait_tolerance_note: The design's staleness limit (72 hours, observed) read at the fixture's one-day resolution: an event is late when it is not handled within 3 days of its arrival day. An event still waiting on the last day is late if those 3 days have run out, and undetermined otherwise.

plans.rule: the mean number of events per calendar day, rounded up to a whole event
nearest-rank quantile of the daily counts
nearest-rank quantile of the daily counts
nearest-rank quantile of the daily counts

plans_sized_on_an_earlier_reading.kind: synthetic: the same assumed rule; each plan is sized on the days read up to a date and run on the days that follow
plans_sized_on_an_earlier_reading.note: Every plan above is sized on the same days it is then run on, which no planner can do. To show what that hindsight is worth, each plan is also sized on the days read up to each date of `checkpoints` except the last, then run on the days that follow, starting with an empty queue (which favours the plan).

same_rule_on_the_synthetic_logs.kind: synthetic arrivals and an assumed rule

candidate_logs.kind: synthetic: imaginary summaries classified against the synthetic logs
candidate_logs.note: Imaginary summaries used by one exercise: logs with the observed number of events and days, described only by two measures. Neither exists.

against_the_synthetic_logs.top_4_events: inside the central 95% of the synthetic logs
against_the_synthetic_logs.gini_calendar_days: inside the central 95% of the synthetic logs

transfer_task.kind: synthetic: a hypothetical support desk, not Streeling data
transfer_task.note: Hypothetical support desk for the learner task: tickets opened per day over two weeks. Not Streeling data and not a forecast.

capacity.handling_rule: the rule of scenarios.json, capacity.handling_rule, with tickets for events

plans.rule: the mean number of tickets per calendar day, rounded up to a whole ticket
nearest-rank quantile of the daily counts

checks.check: recount from the event rows equals the counts made by extract.py
the two design files state the number of orphaned triggers that the folder holds
the quietest days and the other days hold all the events
the three formulas for the Gini coefficient agree
adding empty days moves the Gini coefficient by the exact identity G_all = 1 - (m / n)(1 - G_active)
shares of the busiest days never decrease and stay at or below 1
mean times days = events; days above the mean + the others = days
the fourth and fifth busiest days are not tied, so 'the four busiest days' names four dates
the table of days by count covers every day and every event
the Lorenz curve ends at the total
the months partition the log
the last checkpoint is the whole log
percentiles read to date: those of the last reading are those of the whole log, and at every reading they do not decrease with the level and stay at or below the busiest day read
the median is the middle value, or the mean of the two middle values when their number is even; the nearest-rank 50th percentile then takes the lower of the two
moving the day boundary keeps every event
a day boundary moved by 0 hours reproduces the UTC daily counts
negative control: a boundary moved by a whole day shifts the dates and changes no count
the two type subsets are disjoint and hold every event between them
the events of the four busiest days, split by type, add up
each pair of busiest days lies inside one episode of burst days, the two pairs inside different episodes, and the episodes hold every burst day once
every event has the same repo and ref, so the type is the only part of the deduplication key that varies
merged triggers: at least one on every active day and never more than the number of types
the wait tolerance in days is the design's staleness limit in hours
capacity accounting: handled + left = arrivals; on the day + later + late = handled
a capacity equal to the busiest day leaves nothing waiting
more capacity never makes more events late
the smallest sufficient capacity is exact: no late event with it, at least one with one unit less
negative control: with no capacity nothing is handled and every event is left
a reading date splits the log into days read and days left, and neither part is empty
days left: no late event with their smallest sufficient capacity, at least one with one unit less
every synthetic log has the observed number of events and days
the synthetic batch has the stated number of logs
known answer: the batch mean of empty days is the exact expectation n ((n - 1) / n) ** T, within tolerance
the replication batch (another seed) agrees with the main batch within the stated tolerance
negative control: the observed log, added to the batch, is counted once by every comparison
hand-computed case: the Gini coefficient and the share of the busiest day are the values worked by hand
all days equal gives a Gini coefficient of 0
everything on one day of n gives a Gini coefficient of (n - 1) / n
synthetic logs with a late event: none when the largest number of late events is 0, more than half of the logs when the median number is above 0
the capacity rule reproduces the case worked by hand
transfer task: one unit of capacity less than the smallest sufficient one leaves a late ticket
